haiku-low.q1: Gateway returns 401 Unauthorized. Redis is not called and no budget is used.
haiku-low.q2: Keys share one budget per customer per minute: 100 requests/minute for Standard. Enterprise limit is an open question, not set.
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests plus Retry-After. The backend never sees the request.
haiku-low.q4: No. A rejected request does not increment the count.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. Counting happens inside check_and_incr before forwarding, so the request still counts.
haiku-low.q6: It fails open: one attempt, 50 ms timeout, no retry. The request is forwarded, not counted, with no X-RateLimit headers, and a metric is emitted.
haiku-low.q7: Standard: 100 requests/minute. Enterprise: NOT STATED (open question, no limit set).
haiku-low.q8: One Redis counter per customer per minute, key rl:{customerId}:{minute}. Redis deletes each key when its 120 s TTL expires.
haiku-low.q9: Fixed one-minute UTC-aligned windows. Each new minute uses a new key starting at 0, so the budget resets then.
haiku-low.q10: check_and_incr is one Lua script that Redis runs atomically, one script at a time, so two instances cannot both take the last slot.
haiku-low.q11: Seconds left until the current minute ends, rounded up, minimum 1.
haiku-low.q12: No retry; one attempt with a 50 ms timeout. The client gets the response with no X-RateLimit headers.

sonnet.q1: Gateway returns 401 Unauthorized. Redis is not called, so no counter or budget is affected.
sonnet.q2: Only one shared budget: counters are keyed by customer ID, not API key, so all three keys share it (Standard plan: 100 requests/minute total; Enterprise limit not set).
sonnet.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header. The backend never sees the request.
sonnet.q4: No. On rejection the count is not incremented.
sonnet.q5: Yes. Counting happens in check_and_incr before forwarding, so a request still counts if the backend returns 500.
sonnet.q6: Gateway emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric and forwards the request anyway (fail open). It is not counted, and the response has no X-RateLimit headers.
sonnet.q7: Standard = 100 requests/minute. Enterprise = NOT STATED (open question; Product has not decided).
sonnet.q8: In one shared Redis used by all 6 gateway instances, one counter per customer per minute, key rl:{customerId}:{minute}. Redis deletes each key when its 120 s TTL expires; nothing else removes them.
sonnet.q9: At the start of each new fixed one-minute UTC clock window (minute taken from Redis's clock). A new minute uses a new key, so the count starts at 0.
sonnet.q10: check_and_incr is a single Lua script that Redis runs atomically (one script at a time), so two instances can never both take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: Seconds left until the current minute ends, rounded up, minimum 1.
sonnet.q12: No retry: one attempt with a 50 ms timeout. The client gets the backend response with no X-RateLimit headers, since the count is unknown.
